mutations.label: the provider's own enumerated values stop surviving, so `order_by=created_at_desc` becomes a synthetic string and four list operations replay 400 — a divergence the sanitiser manufactured
a path the document does not describe keeps its segments, so a bucket name and a DNS zone are published because they looked like ordinary words
the same original stops getting the same replacement, so the identifier a create answered is not the one the read addresses and the transcript stops referring to itself
a UUID is replaced by a bare token instead of a UUID, so every read that follows answers 404 and the corpus is a museum piece
an OpenSSH key is replaced by a token, so sshkey.Parse refuses it and every create carrying one answers 400
the bound on a kept run of digits goes, and Outscale's twelve-digit account number is published as a page number would be
the cross-reference against the source recording stops comparing, so a value the sanitiser failed to recognise is published and the file still reads as sanitised
THE COMMAND: the audit no longer stops the write, so the leak is published before it is reported
the alphabet accepts anything, so a value no rule of this package could have produced passes the scan of a committed artefact
mutations.find: return "not a value a sanitised transcript may carry"

mutations.label: the User-Agent is replaced wholesale, so a sanitised corpus can no longer say which client called an operation and `coverage --observed` loses its column
a pack may vouch for an identifier, and every occurrence of it is then published verbatim while the file still reads as sanitised
THE OTHER DIRECTION: what a pack vouches for stops being kept, so the zone in every recorded path becomes a synthetic string, the emulator answers 400 unknown zone, and the corpus is unreplayable

the IPv6 block counter lands in the bits the prefix mask erases, so every /64 of a recording becomes one block and the corpus states #270's own finding — two networks sharing a prefix — as an artefact of the instrument
